overall: Reissued on reconsideration (Feb. 18, 2020) to correct a staff title: the Board approved Feb. 13, 2018 executive session minutes late and inaccurately (intentionally), and Gillespie's email was an OML deliberation.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Board did not approve its Feb. 13, 2018 executive session minutes in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: Here, despite meeting more than a dozen times in the intervening months, the Board failed to approve minutes for its February 13, 2018, executive session until October 9, 2018.

allegations.summary: Alleged a discussed topic was removed from the Feb. 13, 2018 executive session minutes before approval. Found inaccurate and approved intentionally.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the minutes of the February 13, 2018, executive session, as approved, were inaccurate because they failed to summarize a topic that was discussed.

allegations.summary: Alleged then-Selectman Gillespie deliberated outside a public meeting via an email asking that a topic be removed from the minutes.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that selectman Gillespie’s email copying Chair Boshart constituted deliberation outside of a public meeting, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Each Board member must attend a comprehensive Open Meeting Law training (DOG monthly webinar or training by Board counsel) and certify to the AG within 60 days of receipt of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar violations in the future may result in the imposition of a civil penalty.
